subject: Super El Niño
query: what is a super el nino
title: What is a super El Niño? The record 2026 event, explained
answer: "Super El Niño" is the informal name for a very strong El Niño, when sea-surface temperatures in the central Pacific's Niño 3.4 region run more than 2.0°C above normal. The 2026 event set a record: the daily anomaly hit 3.11°C on Sept. 21, 2026, beating the previous high of 3.08°C from Nov. 18, 2015.
body:
El Niño (also spelled El Nino) is a natural warming of the tropical Pacific that shifts weather worldwide. Scientists grade it by how far the Niño 3.4 region runs above average: weak at 0.5°C, moderate above 1°C, strong above 1.5°C and "very strong" above 2.0°C. "Super El Niño" is not an official category, but it is widely used for the very strong events of 1982-83, 1997-98 and 2015-16.

The current event began in June 2026, Carbon Brief reported, and by August the monthly anomaly was about 2.45°C, above the peak of every earlier event except 2015-16 (2.75°C). Fourteen seasonal models projected a peak of about 4.1°C later in 2026. El Niño usually peaks in November or December and is expected to last into 2027, when most of its effect on global temperatures will be felt.
in_the_news: Forecasters say the record 2026 El Niño is near its peak heading into winter 2026-27.

faq.q: Is El Niño 2026 a super El Niño?
faq.a: Yes, by the usual informal definition: its Niño 3.4 anomaly passed 2.0°C and set a daily record of 3.11°C on Sept. 21, 2026.

faq.q: What does a super El Niño mean for winter?
faq.a: Strong El Niños tend to shift storm tracks; NOAA and local forecasters publish regional winter outlooks.

faq.q: When was the last super El Niño?
faq.a: 2015-16, which peaked at a monthly anomaly of about 2.75°C. Earlier ones were 1997-98 and 1982-83.

faq.q: How long will El Niño last?
faq.a: The 2026 event began in June and is expected to last into 2027.

faq.q: What is the difference between El Niño and La Niña?
faq.a: El Niño is unusual warming of the tropical Pacific; La Niña is unusual cooling.
